# PDF library notice and corresponding source

Aurora uses iTextSharp.LGPLv2.Core 3.8.6, an unmodified LGPL-2.0-only library by Vahid Nasiri and the original iText contributors (Bruno Lowagie, Paulo Soares and others). Aurora original code remains MIT licensed. The library license, copyright notices and other dependencies retain their own terms. There is no warranty for the library. See the full LGPL text in the offline Licenses and notices view and the source archive's LICENSE.md and source headers.

Modification for your own use and reverse engineering to debug those modifications are permitted. Nothing in Aurora's terms restricts those LGPL rights. No production signing key or Google credential is required to modify the PDF engine.

## Materials supplied with each release

The release must offer `aurora-corresponding-source.zip` alongside its installers/APK, at the same download location and with equivalent access. That archive contains the corresponding Aurora source/build scripts, this guide, a per-file SHA-256 manifest, and the complete unmodified upstream library archive under `third-party/sources/`. Do not publish binaries without that matching source asset. A link to a moving upstream branch is not a substitute. Offline redistribution must include this source asset too.

The upstream commit is `8f62a2d7be211c4ca9b5bfb953c7443daeeb609c`. `third-party/sources/manifest.json` records the exact source archive and published NuGet package hashes. Source has not been modified by Aurora. The archive includes the upstream project, embedded font resources, build configuration and signing material supplied publicly by upstream. Retain its notices in any modified distribution.

## Rebuild and relink

1. Extract the corresponding Aurora source archive. Install the .NET 10 SDK used by the checked-in build workflows. Native app builds also need the MAUI workloads and Windows/Android SDKs described in README.md and the checked-in build workflows.
2. Extract the nested library source archive to a separate working directory. Edit its source. From that directory build its project with `dotnet pack src/iTextSharp.LGPLv2.Core/iTextSharp.LGPLv2.Core.csproj -c Release -p:TargetFrameworks=net10.0 -p:PackageVersion=3.8.6-local.1 -p:GeneratePackageOnBuild=false -o ./local-packages`. The upstream project includes its public strong-name signing key; this is not Aurora's private distribution key. Keep the assembly identity if relying on binary replacement.
3. In Aurora, change the `iTextSharp.LGPLv2.Core` PackageReference versions in Aurora.Documents, Aurora.Logic, Aurora.Web, Aurora.Tests and Aurora.Legacy to `3.8.6-local.1`. Add the absolute local-packages directory to a local NuGet.Config packageSources list, retaining nuget.org and the absolute vendor/nuget directory. Then restore with `dotnet restore Aurora.Tests/Aurora.Tests.csproj --configfile <local-NuGet.Config>` and use the same config for the native app restore. Version changes avoid NuGet's cache for the original published package.
4. Rebuild Aurora against your modified library. For Windows use the publish options in `.github/workflows/build-windows.yml`, targeting win-x64. A modified local Windows build can run unsigned. For Android use the Android build workflow and your own signing key. Android's signature rules require a separately signed build to be installed under a different application ID or after explicitly backing up and removing a differently signed installation; those rules do not prevent rebuilding/relinking. Do not remove an existing installation merely to test a library change.
5. Run `dotnet test Aurora.Tests/Aurora.Tests.csproj -c Release -m:1 --filter "FullyQualifiedName~PdfExportAcceptanceTests|FullyQualifiedName~CharacterSheetFlatteningTests|FullyQualifiedName~SrdBaselineAcceptanceTests|FullyQualifiedName~SrdSpellBaselineTests"`. Export synthetic sheets and review their rendered pages before relying on modified output. Android PDF export uses portable fonts and Save, Share and Open actions. These source-native tests validate the shared engine; native delivery acceptance is recorded separately.

The native application source and source-native PDF tests are included. Historical oracle binaries and saved-character fixtures containing imported non-SRD descriptions are omitted; neither is needed to rebuild or relink the application. The selected tests above create synthetic characters and use the bundled SRD resources. Full historical parity runs require the separate repository fixtures and oracle prerequisites. The old AGPL iTextSharp 5 dependency is omitted and is not a runtime dependency of the migrated app.

Google credentials, private signing keys and the production release/signing workflow are intentionally absent. The ordinary Windows/Android build workflows are included for rebuilding with your own configuration. To exercise your own Drive account, prepare your own client configuration as documented. Native unsigned/local test builds do not require Aurora's production keys. Vendored Aurora.Content packages and their explicit MIT grant are included.
